deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a short philosophical excerpt and paraphrase of J. F. Herbart's psychology, with Riemann's own glosses. The folio number 136 is circled in the right margin, and the upper right corner is marked 'Riemann 18'.

Content, restated:

(0) Herbart starts from the investigation of the 'Ich' (the self, the problem of 'Ichheit'). From this follow 'psychological postulates'. Their explanation must be sought in the constitution and sequence of the presentations (Vorstellungen). That constitution must necessarily be presupposed, and is therefore knowable through this requirement.

(1) Opposition and mutual exclusion of the presentations, i.e. presentations inhibit each other. The key idea is that presentations themselves act as forces. Riemann calls this the foundation of all psychology. It replaces the supposed separate faculties of the soul, which are only general names for groups of similar phenomena. The temporal succession of presentations belongs here as a condition of selfhood. Without it only a static equilibrium of all presentations among one another could arise.

(2) The concept of negation must be attached to those presentations that are to count as images (Bilder). But negation, like every other concept, is not originally available and must be generated. General negating arises from the many mutual cancellations (Aufhebungen) of presentations.

(3) A pure position, the 'Real' (Herbart's metaphysical simple being), must be attached to the images as images. Riemann's parenthesis apparently calls it the inner principle of their negatability.

(4) This Real of the images must be located in the series of the rest (of what exists or is depicted), for the purpose of subsumption.

My interpretive note: the 'statics' versus succession remark alludes to Herbart's statics and mechanics of the mind (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 1824–25). Herbart's mathematical psychology of inhibition sums and equilibria underlies what Riemann discusses elsewhere in his natural-philosophy fragments. Nothing on this page develops that mathematics.
errors: No mathematical steps to check. As a summary of Herbart's doctrine the content is faithful in substance: presentations as forces that inhibit one another, rejection of faculty psychology, and the problem of the Ich. The numbered 'postulates' 2–4 (negation, position/Real, subsumption) look like Riemann's own reorganisation of Herbart's analysis of the self-image problem, not a verbatim quotation.

results.what: Presentations (Vorstellungen) treated as mutually inhibiting forces as the foundation of psychology, replacing faculty psychology; succession in time as a condition of the self rather than static equilibrium
results.modern_name: Herbartian psychology (statics and mechanics of presentations); associationist and dynamical models of mind
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (Lehrbuch zur Psychologie 1816; Psychologie als Wissenschaft 1824–25)

results.what: Concept of negation not innate but generated from the mutual cancellation of presentations; position/Real attached to images
results.modern_name: Herbartian epistemology / theory of concept formation
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart; Riemann's engagement documented in his 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' (Werke, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's adherence to Herbart is well known: he wrote 'Der Verfasser ist Herbartianer in Psychologie und Erkenntnisstheorie', published in the Werke, and scholars such as Scholz and Ferreirós have discussed this influence. This page is a reading note on Herbart's psychological postulates, with no mathematics and nothing unexpected.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Hier-[?]' is a hyphenation across the line break, probably 'Hier-aus' (continuing 'aus ergaben sich ihm…').

'statt aller vermeinten Seelenkräfte[?]': the word is hard to read. Herbart's standard target is 'Seelenvermögen', so 'Seelenvermögen' or '…kräfte' are both possible; the image seems to end in '-kräfte'.

'Es gehört dazu das Verschmelzen[?]': the image shows corrections and strike-throughs here. The surviving reading seems closer to 'Es gehört dazu das Vorhergehende(?) / die Zeitfolge der Vorstellungen'; 'Verschmelzen' is uncertain.
Item 2: 'als' in 'welche als Bilder gesetzt werden sollen' is underlined in the manuscript; 'ursprünglich bereit[?]' may read 'ursprünglich in Bereitschaft' or similar.
Item 2: 'allgemeine' in 'Das allgemeine Negiren' is underlined.
'psychologische Postulate' is underlined in the manuscript.
Item 4: 'dort[?] der sie, und abgebildet werde' is uncertain; perhaps 'das da ist, und abgebildet werde' or 'das da sei, und abgebildet werde'. 'Sub-sumtion' is correct.
Item 3: '(als das innere Princip ihrer Negirbarkeit[?])' – the last word is uncertain (possibly 'Negation' or 'Nothwendigkeit').
